scope: Read-only interpretation of existing browser telemetry, exact-hash run records, event samples, direct same-RAF captures, and media metadata. No recording was rerun. This does not establish continuous collision detection, physical contact, autonomous intelligence, human acceptance, or physical performance.

motionEnvelope.clock: Normal browser requestAnimationFrame and performance.now; UI controls with condition waits; no accelerated step.
motionEnvelope.durationNote: The uncut MP4 transcode is 0.5483 s shorter than the telemetry duration; event times are telemetry clock values, not exact MP4 frame times.

autonomyDefault.clock: performance.now real time; no accelerated step or user controls during recording.

autonomySeeded122s.clock: performance.now real time; no accelerated step or user controls during recording.
autonomySeeded122s.tailNote: The rail-press/right-sweep planner label begins at 120.6111 s and remains selected at 122.015 s. The final sample is state=watch and contact=false; no executed or completed action is established in this tail.

retainedShortPrecursor.status: Retained precursor; superseded by the 122 s seeded capture for a complete 120 s video comparison.

recordings.samplingCaveat: The telemetry samples at roughly 10 samples/s while the autonomy MP4 transcodes are about 30 frames/s. Zero hidden telemetry samples means the recorder did not count hidden samples; it does not mean every video frame has a metrics sample or prove continuous acting between samples.

autonomousSequences.interpretation: actionFamily and beatId are planner/current-beat labels in telemetry, not proof that an action executed or completed. The counts below are label onsets only. Execution evidence is reported separately as state samples and software contact-flag intervals; no automatic pass for behavioral variety or acting is inferred.
autonomousSequences.windowMeaning: Label windows run from one recorded family/beat label onset to the next, or to the last telemetry sample. They do not describe a continuous executed action duration.
autonomousSequences.contactMeaning: Recorded software contact flag / detector state. Intervals below are consecutive telemetry event samples with contact=true, ending at the first recorded false sample; they do not prove physical contact or continuous collision detection.

default.repeatedBeatLabel: edge-probe / back-corner-right is selected twice; the repeated label alone does not establish two completed actions.
default.stateCoverage: Samples include watch, pace, boundary, cage-test, recover, agitated, settle, and claw-scrape states. These sampled controller states are not a behavior-quality or human-acceptance pass.

familyBeatLabelWindows.executionStatus: planner label remains selected; action execution/completion is not established by this tail

seeded122s.repeatedBeatLabel: rail-press / right-sweep is selected twice across the full capture. Only its first onset falls within the comparable first 120 seconds; the second begins at 120.6111 seconds and remains in state watch with contact=false through the last sample, so it is not counted as an executed action.
seeded122s.stateCoverage: Samples include watch, pace, boundary, cage-test, recover, agitated, settle, and claw-scrape states. These sampled controller states are not a behavior-quality or human-acceptance pass.

mechanicRoutine.qualification: The stop event requests stopping after a cycle; samples continue through release/settle/dwell until the recorded 14-step state is ready.

visitorBillContact.qualification: A short software bill/rail contact flag was observed in two telemetry samples; this is not evidence of continuous collision checking or physical impact.

directActionCaptures.method: Rendered canvas and metrics read in the same RAF callback; normal-clock scripted controls.
directActionCaptures.alignmentLimit: These capture-time values belong to the scripted direct-action run, not exact frame offsets within any uncut video. Earlier video-seek PNG extractions are approximate; they are not used to infer event timing.

limits: Telemetry and event timestamps describe the exhibit's software state and sampled motion. They do not prove continuous acting or collision between samples.
Recorded contact flags use the app's geometric detectors and do not establish a physical object, force, impact, or safe operation.
The capture proves local normal-clock browser execution against the exact GLB hash. It is not a physical-device, constrained-network, deployment, or artistic-acceptance result.
result: Two complete normal-clock no-input autonomy captures cover 120.033 s and 122.022 s of MP4 respectively; the later explicitly seeded capture starts at motionTime 0.1601 s and supplies the full-duration seeded comparison. The shorter 119.964 s predecessor is retained and marked superseded for that comparison. The envelope records the requested era/action/inspection sequence, with video/telemetry duration mismatch and sampled-contact limits stated above.
